requirements.quote:
Errors that result in the connection being unusable, such as an
   obvious violation of protocol semantics or corruption of state that
   affects an entire connection, MUST be signaled using a
   CONNECTION_CLOSE frame (Section 19.19).
requirements.condition: An error makes the connection unusable, including an obvious protocol-semantics violation or connection-wide state corruption.
requirements.required_behavior: Signal the error using a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not leave such a connection error unsignaled or signal it only through a different frame type.
requirements.error_behavior: Use a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame to signal the connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can induce a connection-fatal error and inspect whether the endpoint emits a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.

requirements.quote:
Application-specific protocol errors are signaled using the
   CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with a frame type of 0x1d.  Errors that are
   specific to the transport, including all those described in this
   document, are carried in the CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with a frame type
   of 0x1c.
requirements.condition: The endpoint signals an application-specific protocol error.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the error in a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame whose frame type is 0x1d.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode an application-specific protocol error using CONNECTION_CLOSE frame type 0x1c.
requirements.error_behavior: Signal the application-specific error with CONNECTION_CLOSE frame type 0x1d.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted CONNECTION_CLOSE frame type can be decoded and compared with the error category.

requirements.quote:
Application-specific protocol errors are signaled using the
   CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with a frame type of 0x1d.  Errors that are
   specific to the transport, including all those described in this
   document, are carried in the CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with a frame type
   of 0x1c.
requirements.condition: The endpoint signals a transport-specific error, including an error described in this document.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the error in a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame whose frame type is 0x1c.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a transport-specific error using CONNECTION_CLOSE frame type 0x1d.
requirements.error_behavior: Signal the transport error with CONNECTION_CLOSE frame type 0x1c.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted CONNECTION_CLOSE frame type can be decoded and compared with the error category.

requirements.quote:
A CONNECTION_CLOSE frame could be sent in a packet that is lost.  An
   endpoint SHOULD be prepared to retransmit a packet containing a
   CONNECTION_CLOSE frame if it receives more packets on a terminated
   connection.  Limiting the number of retransmissions and the time over
   which this final packet is sent limits the effort expended on
   terminated connections.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives additional packets on a terminated connection after sending a packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Be prepared to retransmit a packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, subject to limits on retransmission count and duration.
requirements.error_behavior: Retransmit a packet containing CONNECTION_CLOSE when further packets arrive on the terminated connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can drop the original close packet, deliver another packet on the terminated connection, and observe whether a close packet can be retransmitted.

requirements.quote:
The only mechanism available to an endpoint that continues to receive
   data for a terminated connection is to attempt the stateless reset
   process (Section 10.3).
requirements.condition: An endpoint continues to receive data for a terminated connection and does not respond by retransmitting packets containing CONNECTION_CLOSE.
requirements.required_behavior: Attempt the stateless reset process if it uses an available response mechanism.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use another response mechanism as an alternative to CONNECTION_CLOSE retransmission for continued data on the terminated connection.
requirements.error_behavior: The available fallback is the stateless reset process.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can continue sending data to a terminated connection and inspect whether any fallback response is a stateless reset rather than another mechanism.

requirements.quote:
As the AEAD for Initial packets does not provide strong
   authentication, an endpoint MAY discard an invalid Initial packet.
   Discarding an Initial packet is permitted even where this
   specification otherwise mandates a connection error.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives an invalid Initial packet, including where the invalidity would otherwise mandate a connection error.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to discard the invalid Initial packet instead of producing the otherwise mandated connection error.
requirements.error_behavior: Discarding the invalid Initial packet may replace generation of a connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can supply an invalid Initial packet and accept silent discard as compliant even when the underlying violation normally causes a connection error.

requirements.required_behavior: Either do not process any frames in the packet or revert all effects of any processing before completing the discard.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard the packet while retaining effects produced by processing its frames.
requirements.why_checkable: State before and after discarding a crafted packet can be compared to verify that frame processing caused no lasting effects.
